# Multi-Stage Dockerfile for Node.js TypeScript Application

## Project Structure
```
project/
├── src/
│   └── index.ts
├── Dockerfile
├── .dockerignore
├── package.json
├── package-lock.json
└── tsconfig.json
```

## .dockerignore
```dockerignore
# Dependencies
node_modules
npm-debug.log*

# Build output
dist

# Development files
*.md
.git
.gitignore
.env*
!.env.example

# Docker files
Dockerfile*
docker-compose*

# IDE / Editor
.vscode
.idea
*.swp
*.swo

# OS
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db

# Test files
**/*.test.ts
**/*.spec.ts
coverage

# CI/CD

```

## Dockerfile
```dockerfile
# ============================================================
# Stage 1: Base — shared foundation for all stages
# ============================================================
FROM node:20-alpine AS base

# Install security updates and required OS packages
RUN apk update && apk upgrade && \
    apk add --no-cache \
        dumb-init \
        curl && \
    rm -rf /var/cache/apk/*

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Create a non-root user early so it's available in all stages
RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && \
    adduser  --system --uid 1001 --ingroup nodejs nodeuser

# ============================================================
# Stage 2: Dependencies — install ALL npm packages
# ============================================================
FROM base AS deps

# Copy package files first (layer cache optimization)
# If these files don't change, npm ci is skipped on rebuild
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./

# Install ALL dependencies (including devDependencies for building)
# --frozen-lockfile ensures lock file is respected exactly
RUN npm ci --frozen-lockfile

# ============================================================
# Stage 3: Builder — compile TypeScript
# ============================================================
FROM deps AS builder

# Copy TypeScript config
COPY tsconfig.json ./

# Copy source code
COPY src/ ./src/

# Run TypeScript compilation
# Outputs to /app/dist by default (configured in tsconfig.json)
RUN npm run build

# ============================================================
# Stage 4: Production Dependencies — install ONLY prod packages
# ============================================================
FROM base AS prod-deps

COPY package.json package-lock.json ./

# Install only production dependencies
# This creates a clean node_modules without dev tools
RUN npm ci --frozen-lockfile --omit=dev && \
    # Remove npm cache to reduce layer size
    npm cache clean --force

# ============================================================
# Stage 5: Runner — minimal final production image
# ============================================================
FROM base AS runner

# Set Node.js environment to production
ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    # Disable npm update checks
    NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1 \
    # Set port (override at runtime)
    PORT=3000

# Copy ONLY production node_modules from prod-deps stage
# (no devDependencies, no TypeScript compiler, no build tools)
COPY --from=prod-deps --chown=nodeuser:nodejs /app/node_modules ./node_modules

# Copy compiled JavaScript from builder stage
# (no TypeScript source files in production)
COPY --from=builder --chown=nodeuser:nodejs /app/dist ./dist

# Copy package.json for runtime metadata (version, etc.)
COPY --chown=nodeuser:nodejs package.json ./

# Switch to non-root user for security
USER nodeuser

# Expose application port
EXPOSE 3000

# Health check — adjust endpoint to match your app
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s \
            --timeout=10s \
            --start-period=15s \
            --retries=3 \
    CMD curl -f http://localhost:${PORT}/health || exit 1

# Use dumb-init to properly handle signals and reap zombie processes
# This ensures graceful shutdown works correctly
ENTRYPOINT ["dumb-init", "--"]

# Start the compiled application
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
```

## Supporting Configuration Files

### tsconfig.json
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "commonjs",
    "lib": ["ES2022"],
    "outDir": "./dist",
    "rootDir": "./src",
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "declarationMap": false,
    "sourceMap": false,       /* Disable source maps in production */
    "removeComments": true,   /* Remove comments from output */
    "noUnusedLocals": true,
    "noUnusedParameters": true,
    "noImplicitReturns": true
  },
  "include": ["src/**/*"],
  "exclude": [
    "node_modules",
    "dist",
    "**/*.test.ts",
    "**/*.spec.ts"
  ]
}
```

### package.json
```json
{
  "name": "my-ts-app",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "tsc --project tsconfig.json",
    "start": "node dist/index.js",
    "dev": "ts-node-dev --respawn --transpile-only src/index.ts",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "lint": "eslint src/**/*.ts",
    "test": "jest"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "express": "^4.18.2"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/express": "^4.17.21",
    "@types/node": "^20.0.0",
    "typescript": "^5.3.3",
    "ts-node-dev": "^2.0.0"
  }
}
```

### Example src/index.ts
```typescript
import express, { Request, Response } from 'express';

const app = express();
const PORT = process.env.PORT ?? 3000;

app.use(express.json());

app.get('/health', (_req: Request, res: Response) => {
  res.status(200).json({
    status: 'ok',
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    uptime: process.uptime(),
  });
});

app.get('/', (_req: Request, res: Response) => {
  res.json({ message: 'Hello from TypeScript!' });
});

const server = app.listen(PORT, () => {
  console.log(`Server running on port ${PORT}`);
});

// Graceful shutdown
process.on('SIGTERM', () => {
  console.log('SIGTERM received, shutting down gracefully...');
  server.close(() => {
    console.log('Server closed');
    process.exit(0);
  });
});
```

## Build & Run Commands

```bash
# Build the image
docker build -t my-ts-app:latest .

# Build with build arguments for versioning
docker build \
  --build-arg BUILD_DATE=$(date -u +'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ') \
  --build-arg VERSION=1.0.0 \
  -t my-ts-app:1.0.0 .

# Run the container
docker run \
  --name my-ts-app \
  --rm \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  -e NODE_ENV=production \
  my-ts-app:latest

# Run with resource limits (recommended for production)
docker run \
  --name my-ts-app \
  --rm \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  --memory="256m" \
  --cpus="0.5" \
  --read-only \
  --tmpfs /tmp \
  my-ts-app:latest

# Inspect image layers and sizes
docker image history my-ts-app:latest

# Check final image size
docker image ls my-ts-app:latest
```

## Size Optimization Summary

| Technique | Impact |
|---|---|
| `node:20-alpine` base image | ~130MB vs ~900MB for `node:20` |
| Multi-stage build | Excludes TypeScript compiler, devDeps, source files |
| Separate `prod-deps` stage | Only production `node_modules` in final image |
| `npm cache clean --force` | Removes npm's internal cache from the layer |
| `.dockerignore` | Prevents large/unnecessary files from entering build context |
| `removeComments: true` in tsconfig | Slightly smaller JS output |
| `sourceMap: false` in tsconfig | Excludes `.map` files from dist |
| Non-root user | Security best practice, no size impact |
| `dumb-init` | Proper signal handling, ~200KB |

> **Typical result:** A full Node.js + TypeScript project often goes from **~1.2GB** (development) down to **~150–200MB** in the final production image.
